_about: Daily aptitude sets for XAT and the BITS Pilani BAAT. Personal settings (state folder, launchd labels, sync folder, a ramp start date) go in config.local.json, which is git-ignored and overrides this file. After editing either, run: python3 apt.py deploy

scoring._source: XAT marking as reported for XAT 2027 (careers360, collegedunia, checked 2026-11-21); BAAT marking is not published

ramp._about: Optional warm-up: from `start`, for `days` days, difficulty moves in a straight line from `from` to `to` (rounded across the whole day, so each day is harder than the one before), overriding the adaptive difficulty. null start = off. Set a start date in config.local.json.

exams.name: XAT 2027
exams.note: Dates from news reports checked 2026-11-21; confirm on xatonline.in

exams.name: BITS BAAT 2027
exams.note: BITS says applications usually open in the last week of November; test date not announced (checked 2026-11-21)

phases.name: xat
phases.label: Mostly Quant, with XAT's other sections until 3 Jan 2027

phases.name: baat
phases.label: Mostly Quant, with BAAT's other sections

exclusive_topics._about: Topics that test the same idea in two places; once one is picked for a day, the others are skipped that day

QA.name: Quantitative Ability
topics: time, speed and distance (including boats and trains)
time and work, pipes and cisterns
number system (divisibility, remainders, HCF and LCM, factors)
QA.guide: XAT Quantitative Ability and BAAT Quantitative Aptitude level: multi-step word problems, not one-formula drills. Hard questions combine two ideas. Use Indian settings and rupees where natural.

DI.name: Data Interpretation
set_kinds: caselet (all data given in a paragraph)
table with some values missing that must be deduced
DI.guide: Each set gives one data source (a table, a chart or a paragraph) with realistic Indian business or public data that you invent. Questions need calculation: growth rates, shares, ratios, averages, comparisons, what-if changes. Never use a real dataset or real company figures.

RC.name: Reading Comprehension
RC.guide: XAT-style passage of 380-480 words, original, dense and argumentative (the author takes a position). Questions test main idea, inference, the author's assumption or attitude, application to a new case, and what would weaken the argument. Wrong options must be tempting: too broad, too extreme, true but not stated, or a reversal.

VA.name: Verbal Ability
topics: vocabulary in context (fill in the blank)
idioms, phrasal verbs and different usage of the same word
VA.guide: XAT Verbal and Logical Ability plus BAAT Verbal Ability. For para jumbles, label the sentences 1 to 5 in the stem and make the options sequences such as 3-1-4-2-5. For sentence correction, quote the sentence in the stem.

LR.name: Logical Reasoning
set_kinds: scheduling across days of the week
distribution of people, items and attributes
LR.guide: BAAT Logical Reasoning topics (puzzles, seating, blood relations, coding, syllogisms, series, clocks and calendars, data sufficiency). A set gives one puzzle with clues; it must have exactly one consistent arrangement, and every question must be answerable from the clues alone.

DM.name: Decision Making
DM.guide: XAT Decision Making: a realistic Indian workplace or social situation with named people, goals and constraints. Ask what the decision-maker should do, which option best balances the stakeholders, or which action is most appropriate. The keyed option is the one a careful XLRI panel would choose: it solves the problem, respects every constraint and stakeholder, and is ethical and practical. Distractors are plausible but break a constraint, ignore a stakeholder, are extreme, or only delay the problem. Numeric caselets must have one computable answer.

AA.name: Analytics Aptitude
topics: systems of linear equations and rank
numerical analysis (bisection, Newton-Raphson, trapezoidal rule, errors)
programming: output of a short program (Python or pseudocode)
programming: loops, recursion and time complexity
AA.guide: BITS BAAT Analytics Aptitude: basic aptitude for computers and mathematics (first-year engineering level). Programs are 4 to 10 lines; write code in the stem with real line breaks and 4-space indentation.
